variants.recon_evidence: The JSON body validator rejects every dotted-quad loopback (127.0.0.1, 127.1, 2130706433) with 422, but a request carrying an IPv6 literal in source_url reaches the media pipeline and the job log shows an outbound socket open at fetch time; the service binds0.0.0.0 with net.ipv6.bindv6only=0.
variants.planner_rationale: Numeric denylist never covers IPv6 text forms; an IPv4-mapped IPv6 literal keeps the socket on 127.0.0.1 while bypassing the dotted-quad filter.
variants.expected_success_signal: Import job returns 200 and the ingested asset bytes match the internal loopback service's index page rather than a rejection
variants.reasoning: The denylist is keyed on dotted-decimal and decimal integers, so a bracketed IPv6 literal is never matched, yet the dual-stack resolver maps ::ffff:127.0.0.1 back to the IPv4 loopback destination. The fetch therefore lands on the internal listener that the application itself can reach but the caller cannot.

variants.recon_evidence: Header X-Fetch-Url drives the headless renderer target. Values starting with http:// are refused by the ingress guard, https://https://evil.test is stripped, but https:internal-renderer.local is accepted and the job record contains a screenshot of that host's dashboard.
variants.planner_rationale: The guard does a prefix compare against the literal 'https://'; omitting the slashes leaves a scheme-relative form that URL parsers still normalise to an absolute https URL.
variants.expected_success_signal: Screenshot job completes with an image of the attacker-controlled page, confirming the renderer fetched a host outside the allowlist
variants.reasoning: Because the check is a string prefix test for https://, the bare scheme plus host slips past, and WHATWG/RFC-3986 parsers used by the renderer treat 'https:attacker.com' as an absolute URL with an authority. The allowlist host comparison is skipped since parsing short-circuits before it.

variants.recon_evidence: Whitelist probe shows links.cdn.trusted.io/ok is fetched while links.cdn.trusted.io.attacker-probe.net also returns metadata, and a Host lookup on that second name resolves to the probe server; the resolver matches on the trusted string being present in the value.
variants.planner_rationale: Substring/label-based allowlist checks are satisfied by making the trusted host a leftmost label, so the registrable domain handed to DNS is still ours.
variants.expected_success_signal: Response body contains the og:title we seeded on our own host while the outbound connect log shows a DNS lookup and TCP handshake to an attacker-controlled address
variants.reasoning: The filter only verifies that the trusted domain appears in the authority string, and prefixing it as the first DNS label satisfies that substring or startsWith-style test. Name resolution and the TCP connection still go to attacker.com, so the fetch lands on infrastructure we control and can fingerprint.

variants.recon_evidence: Cookie preview_url is read during link rendering: setting it to http://127.0.0.1:8080/actuator/env returns the actuator body embedded in the rendered card, while the same cookie set to an unresolvable host returns an empty card. No client-side validation touches the cookie.
variants.planner_rationale: Server-side sink reads the target from an attacker-controllable cookie; reuse the confirmed scheme-parsing quirk against the cookie value rather than a query parameter.
variants.expected_success_signal: Unfurl card embeds our page's title and description, proving the backend dereferenced the cookie-supplied URL server-side
variants.reasoning: The same lenient parser accepts a scheme-without-authority-separator form, so a cookie-borne value reaches the unfurler unfiltered. Confidence is held lower than the query variants because cookie handling can add percent-decoding and length truncation layers that may normalise or cut the value before the parser sees it.

variants.recon_evidence: The catch-all route passes the trailing path segments verbatim to the capture worker; requests for /cdn/screenshot/https://files.partner-cdn.test/a.png render fine, and requests carrying a bracket literal are not rejected by the router or the capture worker, which then shows a cached 2xx from the internal loopback service.
variants.planner_rationale: Path-borne SSRF with no scheme allowlist at all; the only obstacle is the internal denylist, so route around it with an IPv6 mapped literal inside the path segment.
variants.expected_success_signal: Response is a rendered PNG of the internal service root instead of a router400 or a denylist rejection
variants.reasoning: The greedy route forwards the whole tail as a URL, and the mapped IPv6 literal resolves to 127.0.0.1 on a dual-stack host, sidestepping dotted-decimal and integer-based denylists. Confidence is moderated because some routers percent-decode or normalise brackets and colons in path segments, which could corrupt the literal before the worker parses it.
